newsitem.title: USA: Clinton heard "loud pop" as his leg gave way.
newsitem.headline: Clinton heard "loud pop" as his leg gave way.

text.p: President Bill Clinton knew he was in trouble early on Friday when he heard a "very loud pop" in the leg that he had injured skiing a long time ago.

He was going down some steps after a late evening of talk with his host, golf star Greg Norman, looking forward to a big weekend of golf in Florida, far from Washington and the uproar over campaign fund raising.

It was about 1:20 a.m. EST (0620 GMT) and he was walking out of Norman's estate on his way to the cottage where he was to stay overnight. He was talking to Norman when he caught a heel on a step. Doctors would say later that the quadriceps tendon in his right leg popped off the kneecap, crippling the leg.
"He remembers his right leg, his right knee buckling out. He heard a very loud pop and felt some pain in his right leg," White House spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn said.

Norman, no stranger to tragedies involving golf, like the way he lost last year's Masters tournament, came to Clinton's aid as the pain surged. Secret Service agents called an Army physician on duty, William Lang, who quickly determined that the president needed to go to the hospital.

So instead of going to bed, Clinton ended up in an ambulance to St. Mary's Hospital for a closer examination and a decision that he needed surgery. He was loaded onto Air Force One in a wheelchair and flown back to Washington.
Despite the prospect of weeks of rehabilitation, Clinton was trying to remain upbeat.

"I saw Greg Norman this morning. I told him my handicap is going up by the minute," Clinton joked in a telephone conference call from Air Force One to schoolchildren he was supposed to have visited in Jupiter, Florida.
Clinton, an avid jogger, told the students, "I want to be back running soon, and that's encouraging."
It was the same leg that Clinton injured while skiing about 17 years ago. He did not have surgery at the time.
